answer: Imagine your guests getting check-in details, check out times, Wi-Fi info, and answers to common questions automatically, 24/7. This is exactly what we're going to build together today, an Airbnb auto-reply WhatsApp chatbot using only WhatsBolt, no official WhatsApp API needed. Once we've linked our WhatsApp account, we can create our chatbot by selecting the WA chatbot option. Now, let's select the profile where we want to set up the chatbot and click on add item. I've created a document with all the keywords and their respective answers for our Airbnb chatbot, covering details like check-in, check-out, Wi-Fi, and more. We'll keep the status enabled. For not matching default response, choose yes. Then, set recipient type to individual, since we don't want this chatbot replying in group conversations. For type, it doesn't matter in this case because this will be our default response. Give your chatbot a name and a short description. Keywords aren't important in this step, so you can just type any keyword. For presence delay, set it to 3 seconds and enable show typing. This makes it feel like a real person is responding. Now, let's set the message a user will receive if their message doesn't match any keyword. In our case, this will act like an index message, listing all the keywords the user can send to interact with our chatbot. As you can see, our message includes all the keywords we want our chatbot to recognize and respond to. And with that, we've completed the first step of our chatbot. Just click submit and our default response is ready. Now, let's create a new item so we can start automating each keyword one by one. This message will handle check-in information. We'll set no match response to no and select individual as the recipient type. Then, we'll add the relevant keywords, in this case, check-in, along with the message the user will receive. Next, we'll add two more items, one for check out information and another for Wi-Fi information. For the Wi-Fi item, we'll also include the keyword internet so the chatbot can respond even if the user types that instead. Now, click the run button to activate the chatbot, and that's it. Now, the action camera manufacturer Insta 360 has launched a new 360° action camera in its X series, the Insta 360 X4 Air. The company has advertised the X4 Air as the lightest ever, 8K 360° action camera in the brand's roster. Dimension-wise, it measures 46 x 113.8 x 37 mm, 1.81 x 4.48 x 1.45 in, and weighs just 165 g, 0.36 lbs, which is almost equal to the smartphone's weight. While shooting at 8K 30 FPS, users can expect a runtime of around 88 minutes. Interestingly, like the X5, the latest X4 Air also supports user-replaceable lenses. On the positive side, it does offer all video modes from the flagship X5 action camera, including 360° video, active HDR, Instaframe mode, time-lapse, loop recording, road mode, and more. Furthermore, it's equipped with Insta 360's flow state stabilization and 360° horizon lock, which handles image stabilization related things. Users can easily auto-edit 360° footage, export videos, and edit images via the Insta 360 app. Unlike the X4, the Insta 360 X4 Air is compatible with most X5 accessories. answer: The iPhone 17 Pro could mark Apple's most daring leap in smartphone photography in years, a claim backed by several compelling leaks. Apple is rumored to equip the device with a brand new telephoto lens offering up to eight times optical zoom, a significant jump from the five times zoom on the iPhone 16 Pro. This would position it to directly challenge Samsung's Galaxy S Ultra series and Sony's Xperia line. What's truly exciting? The zoom isn't expected to rely on digital cropping. Instead, a moving lens element could enable continuous optical zoom, similar to Sony Xperia camera hardware, something Apple hasn't done before. If true, this fusion of hardware innovation and Apple's renowned image processing software could redefine long-range mobile photography. Apple is also reportedly developing a new pro-level camera app, aimed at professionals and photography enthusiasts. This app is expected to offer deep manual control for both stills and video, potentially rivaling Hali, Filmic Pro, and Kino. Whether it's a stand-alone app or a major update to Final Cut's camera capabilities is still up in the air, but it's clearly designed to take full advantage of the new zoom hardware. In addition, the iPhone 17 Pro may feature a physical camera control button on its top edge. This tactile shortcut could launch the camera instantly, making it easier than ever to capture spontaneous moments. A thoughtful touch for users prioritizing photographic speed and convenience. Design tweaks may further highlight Apple's focus on its camera system. Among them, a copper-like color option, a rumored horizontal rear camera bar, and a new triple 48 MP rear camera setup, including 48 MP sensors for the main, ultrawide and telephoto lenses, replacing the previous 12 MP telephoto module with a much higher resolution unit. On the videography side, the Pro model might enable simultaneous front and rear camera recording, a potentially transformative feature for vloggers and content creators wanting to capture their reactions and surroundings at once. All this signals a bold strategy. Apple isn't merely upgrading the camera. It's gearing up for a photography showdown with Samsung and Sony. If that continuous eight times optical zoom pans out, Apple could win over users who've stuck with Galaxy or Xperia specifically for superior zoom. With Apple's finely tuned image processing layered on top, it could deliver long-range shots that rival standalone cameras. Bottom line, the iPhone 17 Pro is shaping up to be Apple's most camera focused smartphone yet. With eight times optical zoom, a pro-grade camera app, a dedicated control button, and 48 MP triple sensors, it promises to blur the line between mobile and professional photography. While we await official confirmation, if these leaks are accurate, Apple may very well set a new standard in smartphone imaging. Finally, what are your thoughts about it? question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: In a dramatic turn of events, billionaire Elon Musk has once again set the internet on fire. This time, by lashing out at a top Trump administration official over a lost government contract. The controversy began when Sean Duffy, the acting administrator of NASA and US Transportation Secretary, claimed that SpaceX, Elon Musk's company, is falling behind on its mission to return humans to the moon. Duffy even hinted that the US government might open the contract to other companies, sparking instant fury from Musk. Within hours, Musk took to his platform, X, formerly Twitter, and launched a series of posts mocking Duffy. He called him Sean Dummy, questioned whether someone with a two-digit IQ should be running America's space program, and then shared a meme with the caption, Why are you gay? That single post went viral instantly, not for humor, but for outrage. Critics accused Musk of being disrespectful, unprofessional, and even homophobic, saying such remarks cross the line for a public figure leading major government projects. Supporters, however, argue that Musk is simply fighting back against unfair government pressure and political bias. They point out that SpaceX has already revolutionized space travel and saved NASA billions through reusable rockets. But the timing couldn't be worse. The US government is reviewing its next phase of moon mission contracts, and Musk's public outburst may further strain his relationship with officials. What began as a corporate disagreement has now become a very public feud, blending politics, ego, and the high stakes of America's space ambitions. Whether Musk's bold defiance helps him or hurts him, only time will tell. But one thing's for sure, when Elon Musk speaks, the world listens, even if it's for all the wrong reasons.

Several days after the start of the crisis, some isolated areas are now getting low on food and drinking water. The relief efforts are inadequate and the regency was not capable of handling this flood and landslide disaster alone. Though more than 1 million people have been displaced, the Indonesian government has so far ignored calls for a state of national disaster to be declared. Those demanding it say the measure would free up resources and improve the coordination of aid. Meanwhile, the government insists that crisis management is done by the provinces and that the 30 million US dollars in emergency funds should be enough, while also promising additional funding if needed. Indonesia has only declared a state of national disaster three times. First, during the 1992 earthquake, then in 2004 when a tsunami killed over 160,000 people, and finally during the COVID-19 pandemic. Some analysts are saying that the government is refusing to do so again to avoid any perception that it can't handle the crisis.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: From album of the year to the biggest stage in sports, Bad Bunny just turned the Super Bowl halftime show into a full-on celebration of Puerto Rico. But one detail from his outfit has fans talking, the number 64 stitched onto his jersey. So what does it mean? The show featured surprise appearances from Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin and transformed the field into a vibrant tribute to Puerto Rican culture. Style-wise, the details were just as intentional. He wore an Audemars Piguet watch, a Marquis diamond stud earring by Marvin Douglas, designed to echo the shape of a football, and a custom white football jersey by Zara. The jersey featured the name Ocasio, a nod to his real name Benito Antonio Martinez Ocasio. And now there's more clarity around the number 64 stitched across his chest. According to Complex, Bad Bunny was paying tribute to his late uncle, who previously played football and wore the same number. Before that detail emerged, fans had floated several theories. Some believed the number referenced his mother's birth year. Others connected it to the initial, widely criticized death toll reported after Hurricane Maria devastated Puerto Rico in 2017. There were even historical interpretations, including a nod to the 64th United States Congress, which passed the Jones-Shafroth Act granting U.S. citizenship to Puerto Ricans in 1917. Some pointed to 2023 when Bad Bunny's Un Verano Sin Ti became the first Spanish language album ever nominated for Album of the Year at the 64th Grammy Awards. At the 2026 Grammys, he made history again, winning Album of the Year for De Mi Tirar Mas Fotos, the first Spanish-language album to ever take home the top prize. That same night, he also turned heads on the red carpet in Schiaparelli's first-ever menswear design, and used his acceptance speech to protest ICE, declaring, we are humans and we are Americans. Those moments echoed into the halftime show, where he appeared to symbolically present his Grammy to a child watching his speech on a small TV, a powerful visual about legacy and representation. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell later praised the artist, saying Bad Bunny understood the weight of the platform and its power to unite people. Ahead of the game, an emotional Bad Bunny said the performance was about joy, culture, and heart, and dedicated it to those who came before him. With this latest confirmation, the meaning appears deeply personal, a family tribute layered into a performance already packed with cultural pride, history, and legacy.

answer: Have you ever noticed how a cat can change your whole world just by curling up in your lap? I want to tell you a story about a little stray named Willow. She wasn't born into a loving home. Born under an old porch, shivering through cold nights, tiny mews barely heard over the rain. Willow's days were spent searching for scraps, darting away from heavy footsteps, wishing for a gentle hand. But the world can be tough for a small cat. One day, she was limping, her paw injured, hungry, and alone. That's when I first saw her, huddled behind a dumpster, eyes wide and scared, but with a glimmer, still hoping someone might help. I remember crouching down, softly calling to her, my heart pounding as she inched closer, cautious. Days of quiet visits, leaving food, just sitting nearby until Willow let me touch her. The first time she leaned into my hand, I felt her whole body sigh. I took her home, cleaned her wounds, and promised she'd never be alone again. But sometimes life isn't fair. Her injury was worse than I thought. The vet said she might not make it. I spent every night by her side, whispering that she was loved, that she mattered. For a while, she got better. She played, purring softly, curling up beside me as if she'd always belonged. One morning, I woke and Willow was gone. Quietly, in her sleep, she'd slipped away, finally safe, finally loved. I still miss her, but for a little while, she found her home. Sometimes that's all any of us need.

answer: Want to sync your Apple Watch or Apple Health data and workouts to Strava? Well, in this video, I'll show you the step-by-step process to connect your Strava account to Apple Health. But before we start with the steps, make sure that you have both the Apple Health and the Strava app on your iPhone, and you log in to your Strava account. The first thing that you want to do is open the Apple Health app. On the Health app homepage, tap on the profile icon in the top right. Under the privacy section, you'll find the apps option. Open it and select Strava. Here you'll see two sections. Allow Strava to write and allow Strava to read. Turn on the toggles below the allow Strava to read section. This allows the Strava app to only read your Apple Health data and not overwrite it. Unless you want that, in which case you can also turn on all. Now, open the Strava app, go to the U section and tap on this gear icon. Now from this list, select manage apps and devices. Under the services section, you'll find the health app. Open it and again tap on the health app and tap on connect. Now from here, you can select what data you want to sync. Allow Strava to write will sync the data from Strava app to the Health app. Whereas allow Strava to read will sync the data from the Health app to the Strava. After making this selection, tap on allow. And now as you can see, Strava is now connected with the Health app. Here it shows a demo activity I just did before syncing. By tapping on import, I can transfer all the workout data from Apple Watch to Strava. You can import all workouts from your Apple Watch for the last 90 days to your Strava account. As soon as the import is finished, reload the activities page and you'll see your workouts on the Strava app. Here is the same activity open on my Apple Watch Series 10. And as you can see, the distance and duration is on point. The calorie burn is also accurate. Apple Watch shows my average pace is 11:53, whereas on the Strava, it shows us 11:52. And the average heart rate is a little bit off. But other than that, the sync is pretty accurate. And that's how you can link or connect your Apple Watch with Strava. If you found this video helpful, then leave a like and subscribe to your Holic for more variable videos. Thanks for watching.

answer: Nvidia's $5 billion Intel bet just became official. Intel confirmed it completed Nvidia's $5 billion share sale on December 26th after regulatory clearance, formalizing Nvidia's roughly 4% stake. What began as a September announcement now sits as settled cash and issued shares on Intel's balance sheet. Nvidia bought 214,776,632 Intel shares at $23.28 each in a private placement. The long-awaited cash infusion landed as a visible vote of confidence, ending months of future tense speculation and transforming a pending deal into finalized ownership. Nvidia's buy-in price was 36% below Intel's prior Friday close, underlining the leverage of a market heavyweight. Early trading showed Nvidia down about 1.7% while Intel stayed mostly flat, as the headline became a routine regulatory filing. The private placement granted Nvidia no special governance or information rights beyond standard shareholders. Federal Trade Commission early termination of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period on December 18th cleared the final regulatory hurdle, shifting the deal from pending to fully done. Jensen Huang described the partnership as historic, noting teams have co-developed architecture across CPUs, servers and PCs for over a year. He framed the investment as the next step in reinventing computing layers driven by accelerating artificial intelligence demand. Analysts likened the pairing to longtime rivals uniting. Earlier, the federal government engineered a roughly 10% Intel equity stake, signaling industrial policy backing. In President Donald Trump's AI posture, Intel emerged as a corporate vessel for made here ambition. Intel and Nvidia plan to co-develop data center and PC products, including custom X86 CPUs and hybrid system on chips. The deal omits any pledge to move Nvidia GPUs from TSMC. For Intel, the cash and association bolster credibility. For Nvidia, it eases entry into X86 ecosystems.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: The lake gave no sign. For centuries, the waters of Iznik rippled softly against the edge of a city once called Nicaea, birthplace of Christian creed, stage for imperial councils, and grave to forgotten martyrs. Nothing in the breeze, the current, or the reflection hinted at what lay beneath. But in 2014, a drone camera flew low over the water and found a church sleeping just below the surface. 50 meters from the shore, in water barely 3 meters deep, rose the submerged skeleton of a Basilica. Its stone walls followed a familiar pattern, three aisles, east-facing aps, a square narthex, a structure from the early 5th century CE, built shortly after the first Council of Nicea had rewritten the rules of heaven. Scholars now believe it was dedicated to St. Neophytos, a young martyr said to have been killed on that very shoreline, stabbed and abandoned in the shallows for refusing to renounce his faith. The Basilica's shape suggests reverence, but its fate speaks otherwise. In the year 740, an earthquake shattered the region, temples fell, walls cracked, and this church, already fragile on marshy ground, collapsed into the lake and vanished from memory. No chronicler recorded its loss, no pilgrimage map marked its name. For 1,300 years, it lay beneath the water like a cathedral entombed in silence. But even underwater, the clues remained. In 2025, excavators confirmed its identity as the church of the Holy Fathers, possibly built near or over the site of the council itself. Around it, archaeologists found burials, eight tombs lined with terracotta tiles tucked beneath the nave and apse. Infants, children, adults, laid in sacred shadow as if hoping to sleep close to a martyr's bones. And just beyond the ruin a pendant surfaced, its face worn but still clear. St. Nicholas carried by a pilgrim and dropped in reverence or fear. Yet the past here is layered. Beneath the Basilica, some believe are the foundations of a forgotten Apollo temple. Others whisper of a Senate palace where emperor once spoke of salvation. And still others suspect the site predates all of them, a shrine built atop a necropolis, where holiness was measured by how long the dead had waited. No inscriptions remain, no relics speak. Only stones pressed flat by silt and time, held in place by the lake's stillness. But when drought comes, as it has in recent years, the water recedes, the basilica rises again. Columns break the surface, the apse returns to light. For a brief moment, the church is no longer drowned, just exposed. Plans exist now for an underwater museum. Glass walkways suspended above the nave, viewing chambers, lit vaults where visitors may pray or simply witness. But for now, it remains where it was found, submerged, weightless, intact. A sanctuary that did not fall from grace, but was carried into it.

answer: Hello guys. Today, we're taking a closer look at the Hard Hot smartwatch, a product that has been circulating online with bold claims about durability, performance, and reliability. But the real question is, is this watch legit or is it just another online scam designed to grab your money? Let's find out. At first glance, the Hard Hot smartwatch looks impressive. The design is rugged and industrial, clearly aimed at people who work tough jobs or lead active lifestyles. The product page highlights its ultra-durable build, IP68 waterproof rating, and a 14-day battery life. Those features sound appealing, especially when paired with a 90-day money back guarantee. The watch is also marketed as being built for hardworking men and women, which makes it stand out compared to typical fitness watches that lean heavily on lifestyle branding. However, when we dig deeper, some concerns come to light. The promotional material shows features like step counting, weather tracking, and heart rate monitoring, which are pretty standard on smart watches. But there is very little independent information available outside of their own website. A legitimate brand usually has third-party reviews, verified customer experiences on trusted platforms, or at least some level of recognition in the wearable tech space. The lack of transparency makes it harder to trust the claims. Another point to consider is pricing. On the website, the watch is shown as discounted from 139 pounds and 95 pence down to 69 pounds and 95 pence. While discounts are common in online marketing, this style of heavy markdown can sometimes be a red flag, especially when it feels permanent rather than temporary. The flashy promotions like the Father's Day sale banner add to the sense of urgency, which is often used in online sales tactics to push customers to buy quickly without much research. Now, does that mean the hard hat smartwatch is automatically a scam? Not necessarily. The product may very well function as advertised and some buyers could be happy with their purchase. But the lack of verifiable reviews, the generic nature of the advertised features and the reliance on marketing gimmicks should make potential customers cautious. If you're considering buying the Hard Hat smartwatch, my advice is to do your homework first. Look for user feedback outside of the official website, check refund policies carefully and compare it to well-known smartwatch brands in the same price range. It may look rugged and tough, but until there's more independent evidence, it's best to approach with caution. So, is it legit or a scam? The truth lies somewhere in the middle. answer: Meta and Xbox are set to release the Meta Quest 3S Xbox edition, a leaked collaboration that mirrors the strategy seen with the Asus ROG Xbox Ally. This initiative highlights Xbox's ongoing effort to partner with various companies to introduce licensed products into new markets, specifically leveraging Meta's more affordable next-generation VR headsets. The Meta Quest 3S Xbox edition aligns with Xbox's vision of enabling any device, regardless of its native power, to function as a console through cloud technology. The Meta Quest 3S Xbox edition retains the same hardware specifications as the standard Meta Quest 3S. It features RGB LCD panels with a resolution of 1920 by 1832 pixels per eye and a refresh rate configurable up to 120 hertz. The headset is powered by a Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2 SOC with Adreno 740 graphics, 8 GB of RAM, and internal storage options of 128 GB or 256 GB. Are you hungry for the latest news and trends from the internet? Welcome to what's cooking on the internet. Your one stop shop for discovering the hottest digital delights. Hit that subscribe button and let's get cooking. 

Can a viral meme be a form of quiet protest or is it just a silly joke? I think it's a little bit of both. In a world where social media can turn even the most mundane moments into viral sensations, a new app from tech innovator James Steinberg is taking the concept of a meme to new heights. The app lets users change the background of their digital boarding pass to display a now infamous image of Vice President JD Vance as a bald, bearded baby man. It started as a joke, but it's raised some serious questions about freedom of political speech. Steinberg warns users to use at your own risk, but he's already seen hundreds of people use the app to create their own digital boarding passes. The idea for the app came after a Norwegian tourist, Mads Mikkelson, was detained by border control for hours and forced to unlock his phone, which contained the same meme. Mikkelson's entry into the country was denied, and he believed it was due to sensitivities over the doctored likeness of the V. E. Customs and Border Patrol later denied this, claiming that Mikkelson's admitted drug use was the reason for his ejection. Either way, the meme got a lot more traction, raising questions about freedom of political speech. An Irish politician even waved around a printout of the bald Vance meme in parliament while warning of American censorship and repression. In my opinion, it leads to a discussion at the heart of the issue, Steinberg says of his app. But what does this say about our society? Are we using memes as a way to comment on the absurdity of politics, or are we just using them as a way to distract ourselves from the real issues at hand? The project has the approval of Dave McNamee, the creative consultant and humorist in Los Angeles who kicked off the Vance Edits craze back in October of 2024. McName's edits, which included giving Van some more chiseled, Chad-like look, eventually racked up more than 200,000 likes and 16 million views on X. But the real question is, what's the point of all this? Are we using memes as a way to speak truth to power, or are we just using them as a way to mock and belittle those in power? As Steinberg's app continues to spread, it's clear that this is more than just a silly joke. It's a commentary on our society's obsession with social media, our willingness to use memes as a form of protest, and our desire to comment on the absurdity of politics. So, the next time you see a meme, remember, it's not just a joke, it's a reflection of our society's values and priorities.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Xiaomi has introduced the wireless mouse 3 comfort edition, a more ergonomic take on its well-received wireless mouse 3 that arrived back in May. The new version keeps the same hardware, but opts for a wide, sculpted body with a contoured thumb rest for a more comfortable grip. This is a fairly lightweight clicker, measuring 11.89 cm tall and 7.55 cm wide, and tipping the scale at 65 grams. Xiaomi says the new, meticulously sculpted, asymmetrical design is optimized for various hand shapes and should provide more substantial support for the user's palm and fingers compared to its symmetrical sibling. The Pixart 1200 DPI optical sensor is nothing to write home about, but then again, this is an entry-level offering aimed at office use, and the word gaming doesn't appear once in Xiaomi's sales pitch. The dual color matched side buttons on the right side look nice, but they don't appear to be programmable. They're strictly for forward and backward navigation. Xiaomi teamed up with TTC to develop keys, and we're told they offer softer, quieter clicks. The wireless mouse 3 comfort edition also has a new, wider, silicone-coated scroll wheel with precise tactile feedback, and can be paired with up to three devices, one 2.4 GHz wireless connection and two Bluetooth channels. There's no USBC charging. Power comes from a single AA battery with Xiaomi promising months of use on a single cell.

At least 22 people have died and more than 80 more have been injured after a crane fell on top of a moving train carriage in Thailand. It happened near the city of Nakhon Ratchasima. It's around 160 miles northeast of Bangkok. The crane was working on a new rail construction project when it fell and struck a moving train causing it to derail briefly. The state rail authority there has said 195 people were on board. 

At least 32 people have been killed after a construction crane collapsed onto a train in Thailand. Around 80 others have been injured. The crash happened around 150 miles northeast of the capital Bangkok. Our Southeast Asia correspondent Jonathan Head joins us now from the scene. So, Jonathan, what more can you tell us about what happened?

I'm actually standing on the railway line where this happened and behind me they've moved away now using heavy cranes the crushed carriages. If I get the camera operator to tilt up a bit, you can see this is a brand new high-speed line that they're building on top of this existing railway line. And that huge crane you can see above me, that is now tilted at a really dangerous angle. Big parts of it came crashing down, crushing at least three of the carriages, setting one of them on fire. It really was a dreadful scene. They're trying to clear it up now. There are dozens of people still being treated in hospital, and the government has announced what it says will be a very fast investigation into what went wrong. But this is a highly prestigious project. This new railway line is meant to link Bangkok with China. It's part of China's Belt and Road initiative. So it's a very prestigious project and to have such a major disaster happen on it is a real blow to what for Thailand was meant to showcase its modernizing infrastructure. There have, I have to say, been other accidents like this before in Thailand. I think there'll be a lot of skepticism about what kind of action is going to follow this one.

answer: Here are the coolest seven games that you can play on your Apple Watch Series 10. First up, Zombie Overkill. In this shooting game, you are facing off against a horde of zombies in the street. Shoot to kill, defeat all zombies and progress to the next level. You can get more members on your squad and unlock new weapons. The game gets more and more challenging as you move ahead in the game. If you like shooting games, then give it a try. Next up is tap to dash. In this Flappy Bird inspired game, you tap on the screen to dash forward, passing through the open spaces, avoiding the pipes. Quickly pass the obstacle to increase the multiplier and once it reaches five, you get a dash boost. It's frustratingly fun and super addictive. The kind of game that keeps you saying just one more try. Another similar game is Happy Rise. In this one, you have to constantly tap on the screen to keep the bird from falling. You have to go through different obstacles to move ahead and it's much harder than it looks. Apart from the first one, all the other obstacles shuffle around every time you hit the retry. It's a fun but challenging game and I dare you to score just five points on this game. My high score is six. Next up, Hit the Island. It was the first game specifically designed for interacting with the dynamic island. Now, it's also available on the Apple Watch. You have to hit the dynamic island at the top to score points and also save the ball from dropping. You can control the bottom bar via touch or using the scroll wheel. The speed of the ball increases as the game progresses. It's a really fun game. In this 3D game, you play as Dare the monkey. The aim in the game is to collect as many banana coins as you can while avoiding all the obstacles in the way like wooden spikes, big birds, crates, etc. You can control the jump of the monkey through both the touch screen and the crown button. The all-time high score is displayed at the bottom. Mine is 40. Try to beat it. This one is for the bowling fans. The Vegas bowling light is a fun little game. It features a bowling lane with simple graphics, but the gameplay is really fun. Use the scroll wheel to give the ball rotation and just pull back on the screen and release. It also tracks your score just like a real bowling lane and you can compete with in-game characters. Last but not the least, Snake Watch. The classic snake game on Apple Watch. In it, you have to eat as much as you can to grow as large as you can. But beware, if you try to eat any other snake, it's game over. Instead, you can trap them and if they try to eat you, they'll become your food. So, those were seven of the coolest fun games that you can play on your Apple Watch. Let me know in the comments if you have tried any of these and don't forget to like the video, subscribe for Weholic and I'll see you in the next one.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: A World War II themed movie has taken audiences by storm, moving viewers to tears while earning widespread praise from critics and fans alike. Released in 2019, Jojo Rabbit has been hailed as a cinematic masterpiece, one that blends humor and heartbreak in a truly unique way. Directed by Taika Waititi, the film is a satirical coming-of-age story set during the final years of Nazi Germany. At its heart is Jojo, a 10-year-old boy who, indoctrinated by Nazi propaganda, idolizes Adolf Hitler, imagining him as his comical, imaginary best friend. But everything changes when Jojo discovers a Jewish girl hiding in his attic. This discovery forces him to question everything he believes, setting the stage for an emotional and often absurd journey of self-discovery. Viewers have described the film as a powerful blend of laughter and sorrow. One IMDB reviewer wrote, it was hilarious and heartfelt. The acting was superb, the story was thought-provoking. It was funny at times and heartbreaking at others. Another called the film moving, hilarious, tragic, admitting they had doubts at first but trusted Waititi's vision. The emotional roller coaster is real, they added, praising the film's originality and depth. I laughed and I cried, another fan confessed. This film was exceptional, one of the best I've seen this year. Waititi's comedic vision is brilliant, and the cast is phenomenal. The cast includes Roman Griffin Davis in his breakout role as Jojo, Thomasin McKenzie, Sam Rockwell, Rebel Wilson, Stephen Merchant, Alfie Allen, and Scarlett Johansson, with Waititi himself portraying a ridiculous, imaginary version of Hitler. Adapted from Christine Leunens' novel Caging Skies, Waititi initially drafted the script in 2011. Though the original version was much darker, it evolved into a black comedy that could balance satire with genuine emotion. Filming took place in 2018, and the movie premiered the following year to critical acclaim. Jojo Rabbit earned multiple awards, including the Academy Award for best adapted screenplay, making Waititi the first Marry filmmaker to win in that category. Audiences and critics have since labeled it a must watch film, especially for fans of war dramas told from a fresh and human perspective. From laughter to despair, Jojo Rabbit manages to confront the horrors of war through the innocent lens of a child, making it a standout film that resonates long after the credits roll.

This center serves as the starting point for tours and is a resource for visitors with questions about the campus. Harvard is easily accessible by public transit, making it a popular destination for those interested in Boston's rich academic and cultural environment. The self-guided tour app allows visitors to experience Harvard Yard and its surroundings while fitting well into a day spent exploring Cambridge and Boston. To summarize, self-guided tours are available via a free Harvard mobile application focused on Harvard Yard. Official student-led tours requiring advanced registration and have group size limits. answer: The Tesla Cybertruck is one of the most futuristic and talked about electric pickup trucks in the world. The spacious cabin can comfortably seat up to six passengers, making it both a family vehicle and a powerful work truck. The truck also offers strong towing and payload capabilities. It can tow up to about 14,000 pounds and carry heavy cargo in its large rear bed, which Tesla calls the vault. The bed also includes a powered cover to protect cargo and improve aerodynamics. In terms of technology, the Cybertruck comes equipped with Tesla's advanced driver assistance features. This includes autopilot, which can help with steering, acceleration, and braking on highways. Future updates may also enable more advanced self-driving capabilities through software updates. Overall, the Tesla Cybertruck represents a bold step into the future of electric trucks. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer:
What announcement led to the Berlin Wall's collapse?
Imagine waking up one morning and hearing that the border you have been told is closed forever is suddenly open. That's exactly what happened on November 9, 1989, in East Berlin. A government official named Ginter Shabowski held a press conference and announced new travel rules. He said East Germans could now apply for permission to travel abroad without the strict restrictions they had known for decades. But here's the catch. He said the border would be opened immediately or without delay. No one expected such a quick change. People listening to the news thought it meant they could cross the border right away. Thousands of East Berliners flooded to the Berlin Wall, eager to see what was happening. Border guards, overwhelmed and unsure of what to do, eventually opened the gates. This spontaneous movement turned into a mass crossing, and the Berlin Wall, which had divided the city for nearly 30 years, was no longer a barrier. This announcement was part of broader reforms happening across the communist world. East Germany was feeling pressure from internal protests and from the Soviet Union, led by Mikhail Gorbachev, who was pushing for more openness and change. The East German government wanted to ease travel restrictions to calm unrest, but the public misunderstood the scope of the reforms. They believed the border was open for good, which was not exactly the plan. The fall of the Berlin Wall symbolized the weakening of communist control in East Germany and the entire Eastern Bloc. It showed that the socialist governments could no longer hold onto their strict borders or suppress demands for freedom. This event was a turning point that led to German reunification less than a year later, in October 1990. It also marked the beginning of the end for communist rule across Eastern Europe, as many countries experienced their own peaceful protests and reforms. So, the key moment was Ginter Shabowski's announcement during that press conference. It was a simple statement, but it sparked a chain reaction that changed history forever. It was the moment when the people's desire for freedom broke down the physical and political barriers that had divided Europe for so long.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Now deadly flooding in Indonesia has triggered sweeping government action against companies who are accused of worsening the disaster through deforestation. Permits have been revoked, lawsuits filed, and state takeovers threatened. But environmentalists warn the response may fall short and could even put fragile ecosystems at greater risk. After last year's catastrophic floods and landslides in Sumatra that killed more than a thousand people, officials under President Prabowo Subianto acknowledged that deforestation and overdevelopment played a major role in amplifying the disaster. Years of mining, plantation expansion, and forest fires have stripped vast stretches of rainforest across Sumatra, removing trees that once absorbed heavy rainfall and stabilized soil on steep hillsides. Dozens of companies have had their permits revoked, and the government plans to hand management of roughly 1 million hectares of land to a state enterprise. Initially, authorities indicated that the move would include the Martabe gold mine in the ecologically sensitive Batang Toru region, and conservationists have long accused the site of environmental damage. Officials now say that they are still reviewing possible violations, but critics note there's no indication development will halt in Batang Toru. Now, Batang Toru is home to the world's rarest great ape, the Tapanuli orangutan. Fewer than 800 were believed to exist in the wild before the floods. Using satellite data, experts estimate nearly 60 orangutans may have died in what they described as an extinction-level event for the species. Now, between 2001 and 2004, Sumatra lost 4.4 million hectares of forest. That's an area larger than Switzerland, making its landscapes increasingly vulnerable to landslides and flash flooding. Environmental groups warn that transferring land to state control does not guarantee better environmental practices. They say the government has yet to outline clear plans for forest recovery or long-term remediation. Now, lawsuits are seeking nearly $300 million from six companies, some funds earmarked for environmental repair. Experts argue far greater investment will be needed, and more firms may share responsibility.

answer: The pain behind the silence. The root of the unrest. This protest in America didn't erupt overnight. It was born from years of quiet suffering. For decades, millions of undocumented immigrants worked silently. They labored in the fields, cleaned homes, and powered the economy from behind the scenes. Yet, their presence was always treated as temporary, tolerated, not accepted. Then, in early 2025, the US government launched a harsh campaign called the Immigration Dragnet. Raids began in areas densely populated by undocumented workers. Farmers, builders, cleaners, and families who had lived in the country for decades. Homes were stormed, workplaces were invaded. It wasn't just a legal crackdown. It was a message. This country is not yours. That campaign lit a fuse. It started in Los Angeles. A small group of farmworkers walked out onto the streets. Their eyes full of tears, their hands holding signs, their voices trembling with one message. We are human, not illegal. Soon it spread across the country. New York, Chicago, Houston, Sacramento, city after city saw waves of peaceful protesters. They weren't just speaking for themselves. They spoke for the ones who had been detained, the parents separated from children, the silent. The response was brutal. Police fired tear gas, national guard troops were deployed. Mainstream media painted them as threats, as outsiders. But the truth was simple. They were just asking to be treated as people. Dreams, fear, and the road ahead. What now? Now the question stands, where is this going? Some politicians call it a victory for law and order. Others see it as a new face of racial injustice. But for the people on the ground, this is not just about laws. It's about homes, families, and futures. This is a battle for belonging. Experts say, if the movement stays united, if their voices don't scatter, this won't be just a protest, it will become a movement. A movement that could reshape immigration policy and redefine what the American dream truly means. Because the real question is, is the American dream only for those with papers or also for those with calloused hands?

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: From the 12th of October 2025, the EU will introduce new border checks known as the entry exit system, EES. As a part of its plans to strengthen border security, this is a new digital border system that will change requirements for British and other non-EU citizens traveling to the Schengen area, which encompasses all EU countries except for Cyprus and Ireland. It will also include the non-EU states, Iceland, Norway, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein. The entry exit system is an automated IT system designed to register non-EU nationals traveling for short stays of up to 90 days in every 180 days. It will be used every time an individual crosses the external borders of any of the following countries. When EES is introduced, you may need to create a digital record on your first visit to the Schengen area at the port or airport on arrival. This will involve submitting your fingerprints, having your photo taken, and your passport scanned at dedicated booths. This new system will be introduced in phases over the first six months, and will eventually replace the current system of manually stamping passports when visitors arrive in the EU. You will not need to provide any information before traveling. At the port of Dover, Eurotunnel and Folkestone and Eurostar from St. Pancras, EES will be carried out before departure, as is currently the case for border checks. EES may take a few extra minutes to complete, so be prepared to wait during busy times at the border once the system starts. You can check with your travel operator to find out whether EES will affect your journey. Once registered, your digital record will be valid for three years. If you enter the Schengen area again during this time, you will only need to provide one biometric, either a photo or a fingerprint, at the border when you enter or exit. For more information, visit gov.uk/entry-exit system.

answer: The cheetah, a sinonyx jubatus, is a large cat known as the fastest land animal in the world. It has a slender, aerodynamic body built for speed with long legs and a deep chest. Adult cheaters have tan or pale gold fur covered with small, solid black spots all over their bodies, except for the white throat and belly. One distinctive feature is the black tear marks that run from the inner corners of their eyes down to their mouths, which help reduce glare from the sun and aid in focusing on prey. Cheetahs can reach speeds of 93 to 104 km/h, 58 to 65 miles per hour in short bursts covering distances up to 500 m. Cheetahs reside mainly in various habitats across Africa and Central Iran, such as Savannas and arid mountain areas. They play an important role in their ecosystems by controlling prey populations and helping maintain balance. Unlike other big cats, cheetahs have semi-retractable claws which give them better grip, similar to track spikes on running shoes. They primarily hunt during the day and rely on their exceptional eyesight to spot prey from a distance.

answer: Let's take a look at these Adidas men's daily shoes and these are nothing fancy, just the way I like. They just look like a basic skate sneaker with a flat bottom and a wide rubber outsole. The back heel area has an insert that keeps the structure upright and it won't fold like a lot of shoes in this category. And the canvas isn't as basic as you'd think. It feels like it has some kind of coating that provides some rigidity, and it makes them perhaps a little tougher and slightly less vulnerable to getting wet or dirty, but they're definitely not waterproof. Let's put these alongside a pair of Vans. Both are the same size 10 and a half. You can see the Adidas are just a little longer, but you don't really feel it much when you're wearing them because I think most of that length is coming from the padding in the back behind your Achilles and behind the heel. So it pushes your foot forward just a little more than the vans, which have nearly no padding at all in the back. And I'll also mention that they're a little bit wider and honestly, they're a lot more comfortable. But overall, these have been really surprising to me for how good they feel on my feet. That's the final day of the UN's climate change summit, COP 30 in Brazil. Yesterday, the conference had to be evacuated after a fire broke out inside the venue. More than 190 countries have been at the summit in an attempt to strengthen international efforts to address climate change. And on this final day, the delegation from Colombia say that more than 30 countries have signed a letter opposing a draft text because of it fails to refer to the phasing out of fossil fuels. Here's our climate editor, Justin Rowlett. 

The fire is really burning very intensely, burned a huge hole in the roof. The summit was halted yesterday afternoon when a fire broke out in the venue. The intense blaze was swiftly brought under control, but it meant yet another delay in these already fraught talks. They are as much about who isn't here as who is. Secretary General, what message do you want this conference to send to Donald Trump? We are waiting for you. Hope is the last thing that dies. He urged the summit to take bold action. One thing is clear. We are down to the wire and the world is watching Belem. But when the Brazilian President, Lula de Silva flew in, signs of agreement were proving elusive. These talks are being held behind closed doors. The most contentious issues, how to bridge the yawning gap between what countries say they'll do and what the science says is necessary to avoid the worst effects of climate change and how to get rich countries to deliver on promised cash to help poorer countries play their part. The big challenge as always at these talks is that the countries here can't force the others to actually do anything. So if a country doesn't want to phase out fossil fuels rapidly, for example, they don't have to, which means that the outcome of these summits is inevitably always a compromise. And if that compromise isn't ambitious, well, there will be questions about how effective this entire global process is. Justin Rowlett, BBC News, Belem.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Each year in late August, Nevada's Black Rock Desert transforms into a temporary city called Black Rock City. What began in 1986 as a small bonfire gathering on a San Francisco beach is now a global cultural phenomenon. Today, over 70,000 people arrive with tents, bicycles, and art, building a community from nothing but dust. Burning Man isn't just a festival. It's a community shaped by 10 guiding principles: radical inclusion, self-reliance, and self-expression among them. Participants wear futuristic costumes, glittering masks, and LED lights. Strangers become friends, and the desert becomes a place of freedom, creativity, and unity. The playa is a living art gallery. Giant wooden temples tower over the desert floor. Mechanical dragons breathe fire, and surreal neon structures glow against the night sky. Art cars, transformed into moving sculptures, carry dancers and lights through the dust. Everything here is created by participants, and nothing is left behind. From sunrise yoga and meditation to all-night raves, Burning Man pulses with sound and movement. DJs spin under laser beams, drummers pound in circles, and fire spinners light up the night. The energy is raw and electric, a celebration of music, creativity, and life itself in the middle of the desert. At the festival's peak, the Man, a towering wooden effigy, is set ablaze in front of tens of thousands. Flames rise, sparks scatter across the desert sky, and cheers echo through the playa. Another sacred fire consumes the temple, a space for reflection and remembrance. And then, just as quickly, Black Rock City disappears, leaving only dust, memories, and the spirit of Burning Man.

Palace's stance on Guehi will move the chessboard. But if Liverpool choose the high ceiling route, Giovanni Leoni ticks the boxes. Technique, temperament, and tactical fit for a system built on brave defending and faster transitions. Young, fearless, and built for the press. If the Reds make the call, Anfield could be about to welcome its next defensive diamond. Welcome to Liverpool, Giovanni Leoni.

Improved sightlines, a roof packed with giant LED screens, new sound systems and modern access points will change how fans live every match day. Even during construction, supporters can witness the progress through a special viewpoint on a stadium tour. A glimpse of the transformation in motion. The comeback to Camp Nou marks more than just a return to home soil. It's the promise of louder nights, bigger atmospheres and crucially, a new era of financial stability for the club through increased revenue streams. For Barcelona, the message is simple. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to change the font for an entire Google Slides presentation. If you've ever spent way too much time manually updating fonts on each and every slide, I've got some good news for you. This method will help ensure your presentation has a cohesive and professional look throughout, saving you time and frustration. Let's kick things off by opening your Google Slides presentation. Once you're in, take a look at the top menu bar. You're going to click on the slide option. A drop-down menu will appear and from there, you'll want to select edit theme. If you're using an older version of Google Slides, this might be referred to as edit master, but don't worry, it functions in the same way. Once you've accessed the theme editor, you'll see a sidebar on the left side of the screen. Here, you'll notice a series of slide layouts, but what you'll want to focus on is the topmost slide, often referred to as the master layout. Clicking on this slide is crucial as it governs the font and style choices for your entire presentation. Now, with the master layout selected, let's move on to the next step. Look for any text boxes within this slide and select one. You'll then navigate to the toolbar situated at the top of the screen, where there's a whole array of fonts waiting for you. Select the font that best suits your presentation style or your personal preference. Remember, the font you choose will be applied to the whole presentation, so make sure it reflects the tone you want to convey. You'll want to repeat this process for other important layout types. This might include titles, body text, or any other specific layout that's essential to your presentation structure. By ensuring each layout type has your desired font, you'll maintain consistency across your presentation. Once you're satisfied with your selections, it's time to close the theme editor. Simply click the X or close button. You'll find that the new font style automatically applies to all slides that use that particular layout without any additional steps. And there you have it. Your entire deck now has a clean, unified font style, saving you from the hassle of manual edits on every slide. It's really that simple. By following these steps, you not only ensure your presentation is polished and professional, but you also free up your time to focus on content rather than formatting. Thanks for tuning in and I hope you found this tutorial helpful. If you did, don't forget to like, subscribe, and hit the bell icon for more tips and tricks. See you in the next video.

answer: Welcome back to Voltage Learning. Let's walk through this Intel analog engineer question because it touches on a very common bring-up issue that trips up even experienced designers. The question asks, during bring-up, an op-amp configured as a voltage follower shows an output that rails high even when the input is at mid-supply. Which condition most commonly causes this behavior? At first glance, this can feel confusing. After all, a voltage follower is supposed to simply mirror the input. But the key insight here is that negative feedback only works if the op-amp is operating within its valid input range. Even though the circuit uses feedback, the op-amp's input pins still must stay within the device's input common mode range. If the input voltage exceeds that range, often because the op-amp is not rail to rail on its inputs, the internal input stage can saturate. When that happens, the feedback loop effectively breaks down. The op-amp can no longer regulate properly, and the output often slams into one of the supply rails, frequently the positive rail during bring-up. Now, let's briefly rule out the other options. High open loop gain is normal and expected. It doesn't cause an output to rail by itself. Slew rate limits how fast the output can move, not where it settles in steady state. And a lighter output load actually makes it easier for the op-amp to drive the correct voltage, not harder. So the correct answer is, the input common mode exceeds the op-amp's valid range. This is exactly the kind of issue that shows up during early lab bring-up and silicon validation. Intel interviewers like this question because it tests whether you understand that data sheet limits still apply, even in seemingly simple configurations like voltage followers. If you want analog explanations grounded in real world debug scenarios, not just textbook theory, that's what Voltage Learning is built to deliver.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Once upon a time, in the wild landscapes of Tasmania, lived the thylacine, also called the Tasmanian tiger for the dark stripes across its back. Despite its wolf-like face, the thylacine was actually a marsupial, carrying its young in a pouch, just like kangaroos. It was the largest carnivorous marsupial of modern times, a shy and nocturnal hunter that fed on small animals and birds. Unlike dogs or wolves, its jaw could open to an astonishing 80 degrees, giving it a fearsome bite. Sadly, European settlers saw the thylacine as a threat to sheep and livestock. By the late 1800s, there were even government bounties that encouraged hunting. Disease, habitat loss, and competition with dogs only made things worse. The last known thylacine lived in Beaumaris Zoo in Hobart. Filmed in 1933 by naturalist David Fleay, it died just three years later, in 1936. That moment marked the end of a species that had survived for thousands of years. Today, the thylacine remains a powerful symbol of extinction and a reminder of the importance of protecting endangered wildlife before it's too late.

The 32-member alliance emphasized their commitment to Article 5 of the Washington Treaty, that an attack on one is an attack on all, after Trump raised eyebrows by suggesting there were numerous definitions of the clause. However, he later reassured allies saying, "We are with them all the way." Trump celebrated the summit's outcome, calling it a great victory for everyone and a big success. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: What is the Rio de Janeiro International Film Festival? Have you ever wondered what makes the Rio de Janeiro International Film Festival so special? This festival, also known as Festival do Rio, is Brazil's largest film festival and one of the most significant events in Latin America. It started in 1999 when two earlier festivals merged to create a more streamlined event. The Rio Cine Festival, which began in 1984, and the Mostra Banco Nacional de Cinema, founded in 1988, combined to avoid scheduling conflicts and make the festival experience better for everyone. Festival do Rio takes place in the vibrant city of Rio de Janeiro. Each year, it showcases a diverse selection of films, typically featuring over 350 films from more than 60 countries. You can expect to see a wide range of genres, including feature films, documentaries, and short films. The atmosphere at the festival is warm and inviting, making it a great place to enjoy both international films and a broad spectrum of Latin American cinema. One of the standout sections of the festival is called Premiere Brasil. This part focuses specifically on Brazilian cinema and is quite competitive. It features a significant number of Brazilian films, including fiction, documentaries, and shorts. This section provides a fantastic platform for local filmmakers to present their work to both local and international audiences. Attendees often have the chance to meet filmmakers and actors, which adds to the festival's charm. The audience also gets to vote for the best films in various categories, while an official jury awards the festival's main prizes, including the coveted Redentor trophy. The festival is held across multiple cinemas in Rio de Janeiro, making it accessible to a broad audience. In addition to film screenings, Festival do Rio often includes debates, special sessions, and lectures. These events contribute to the cultural and audiovisual development of the city. The festival plays a vital role in strengthening Rio's position in the audiovisual sector and promoting Brazilian culture on both national and international stages. Overall, the Rio de Janeiro International Film Festival is a major cultural event that celebrates cinema, supports local filmmakers, and connects audiences with both global and regional film production. If you are a film enthusiast or just curious about cinema, this festival is definitely worth checking out.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: What is the Adidas Firebird tracksuit? Have you ever wondered how a simple tracksuit became a cultural icon in hip-hop fashion? The Adidas Firebird tracksuit is a perfect example of this phenomenon. Originally launched in the 1980s, this tracksuit features the iconic three stripes along the sleeves and pant legs. It evolved from earlier Adidas styles, such as the Beckenbauer tracksuit, and quickly became a symbol of athletic excellence and street style. The Firebird tracksuit typically consists of a zip-up jacket and matching pants made from shiny polyester fabric. This sleek and sporty look made it a favorite among athletes and fashion enthusiasts alike. In hip-hop culture, the Firebird tracksuit holds a special place as a cultural emblem. During the 1980s, it became closely associated with the emerging hip-hop scene, especially among B-boys, MCS, and break dancers. The tracksuit was embraced for its comfort and durability, which suited the dynamic movements of breakdancing and the expressive fashion of hip-hop artists. One of the most significant moments linking the Adidas Firebird tracksuit to hip-hop came from the legendary rap group Run-DMC from Queens, New York. They famously wore the Firebird tracksuit as part of their signature look, pairing it with Adidas Superstar sneakers and gold chains. This image became iconic and helped establish the tracksuit as the unofficial uniform of old-school hip-hop. Run-DMC's 1986 hit, My Adidas, celebrated the brand and its connection to their identity. This song led to the first major endorsement deal between a music group and a sportswear company, marking a turning point in both music and fashion. The Firebird tracksuit's influence extended beyond just fashion. It symbolized authenticity, street credibility, and unity within the hip-hop community. It bridged the gap between sportswear and music culture, making Adidas a staple brand in hip-hop fashion. Even today, the Firebird tracksuit is revered as a retro classic that represents the roots of hip-hop style. It continues to be worn and celebrated by artists and fans alike. The Adidas Firebird tracksuit is more than just athletic wear. It is a cultural icon that helped define hip-hop fashion in the 1980s and remains a symbol of the genre's early style and attitude.

If the fit is too loose or causes excessive pressure in your ear, try another ear tip size. If you need more grip, use a clean, lint-free cloth to help you remove the ear tip. If you need a different grip, roll the edge of the ear tip inside out, then grip both sides of the ear tip firmly with your fingertips and pull straight out using steady pressure. To attach an ear tip, align it with the oval-shaped connector on the AirPod. Then, push it onto the connector until you hear it click into place. Repeat this process if needed until you achieve the optimum fit. You can also take an acoustic seal test using your iPhone to confirm you're getting the best sound quality and noise cancellation. answer: Lewis Hamilton calls for Africa to take it back as F1 return debate heats up. Seven-time Formula 1 World Champion Lewis Hamilton has made headlines after calling on African nations to take Africa back from former colonial powers, including France, Spain, Portugal, and Britain. Hamilton made the comments while responding to a South African journalist who asked about Formula 1's long-awaited return to the continent. The sport has not held a race in Africa since the 1993 South African Grand Prix at Kyalami. The British racing icon revealed he has been pushing for years to bring Formula 1 back to Africa and says he won't retire until it happens. I've been fighting for the past six, seven years to get the sport back there. Hamilton said, making it clear that a race on African soil is a personal mission for him. Opening up about his heritage, Hamilton added, I'm half African. I've got roots from Benin, Senegal, Nigeria. It's something I'm really proud of. He went on to speak passionately about the continent's future, saying he believes Africa has the potential to be the greatest and most powerful place in the world because of its vast natural resources. However, he also expressed frustration about foreign influence over African economies and leadership structures. I don't like that the rest of the world owns so much of it and takes so much from it and no one speaks about it, he said. I'm really looking forward to hoping that the people running those different countries unite and take Africa back from the French, from the Spanish, from the Portuguese and the British. Hamilton has frequently visited Africa in recent years. During his 2024 mid-season break, he spent significant time in Senegal, describing the trip as heavy but deeply meaningful. He said it was important to learn history and honor the people and cultures his family roots trace back to. Beyond his activism, Hamilton is also preparing for the start of a new Formula 1 season, with the opening race set to take place in Australia this weekend. He marked race week with a shirtless Instagram post captioned, Race week, I'm ready. Off the track, Hamilton has also been making headlines for his personal life. Reports suggest he has recently been spending time with reality TV star Kim Kardashian. The pair were reportedly seen together at an exclusive desert destination near the Colorado River, close to the ultra-private Amangiri resort. The luxury hideaway is known for attracting high-profile celebrities seeking privacy with suites costing thousands of dollars per night. According to reports, Hamilton and Kardashian were spotted taking a cozy selfie before leaving in a black SUV. The sighting follows their joint public appearance at the Super Bowl last month, fueling speculation that their relationship may be getting serious. As the new F1 season begins, Hamilton is once again in the spotlight, not just for his racing ambitions, but for his outspoken views on heritage, global politics, and representation in sport. Whether it's campaigning for Formula One's return to Africa or navigating high-profile romance rumors, Lewis Hamilton continues to make an impact both on and off the track.

answer: For decades, fusion energy, the process that powers the sun, has been one of science's greatest opportunities. Cracking it would give us a safe, clean, and virtually unlimited source of power. Controlling plasma hotter than the sun's core means solving physics so complex that even the fastest supercomputers struggle to simulate it. At the forefront of this effort, General Atomics researchers and international partners at the D3D National Fusion facility are using AI to push fusion research forward. The team is building a fully interactive digital twin of the D3D Tokamak inside NVIDI Omniverse. It fuses sensor data, physics simulations, engineering, and AI models, creating a virtual reactor that can quickly inform decisions. Key controls can be explored in the digital twin to refine the science before running real experiments. These surrogate models trained on decades of real-world data sets and running on NVIDI GPUs deliver accurate predictions at unprecedented speed. This is a platform to optimize reactor designs, accelerate commercial fusion, and make the sun's power programmable.

Starting at around $80,000 for the standard O-wheel drive model and topping out near 117,000 for the Cyberbeast True. The Cybertruck positions itself as a premium electric pickup. The exterior is built from what Tesla calls hard freaking stainless, a proprietary cold rolled stainless steel alloy that's roughly 1.8 mm thick on the doors and 1.4 mm on the body panels, Capital 1. This isn't just for looks. The material resists dings and dents far better than traditional sheet metal, Capital 1. Though you'll need to baby it a bit since it can still scratch and pick up surface contamination. The Cybertruck features steer-by-wire technology and four-wheel steering, Tech Times, making this massive truck surprisingly maneuverable in tight spaces. Under the angular body, you'll find an 816-volt battery pack with a capacity of 123 kilowatt hours, Wikipedia. Range varies from 318 to 340 miles, depending on configuration, Cars. And when you need to charge, the system can add significant range in just 15 minutes at high-powered stations. Performance is where this truck gets genuinely wild. The all-wheel drive version pumps out 600 horsepower and sprints to 60 miles per hour in just 4.1 seconds. While the top tier Cyberbeast cranks out 845 horsepower and hits 60 in a blistering 2.6 seconds, Kelly Blue Book. Yes, you read that correctly. This is a full-size pickup truck that accelerates faster than most sports cars. Both versions can tow up to 11,000 pounds and handle payloads exceeding 2,200 pounds, True car. So it's not all show and no go. Inside, minimalism reigns supreme with an 18.5 inch central touchscreen, controlling virtually everything. Torque you from climate to suspension height. Rear passengers get their own 9.4 inch screen, and the cabin features a 15 speaker audio system, Cars. The interior embraces utility over traditional luxury with durable materials designed to handle real work and play. The bed measures 6 ft by 4 ft with 67 cubic feet of cargo space, Cars Direct, and the composite construction keeps things practical. There's even a wade mode that lets you cross water up to 2 and a half feet deep, Wikipedia. Perfect for those off-road adventures. Safety tech includes adaptive cruise control, automatic emergency braking, and blind spot monitoring, True car, with Tesla's full self-driving system available as an $8,000 option. The Cybertruck represents Tesla's bet that the future of trucks doesn't have to look like the past, and whether that gamble pays off depends entirely on whether you're ready to embrace something radically different.

answer: The VDNKH robot, the Soviet Android dream. Soviet engineers created humanoid robots in the 1950s that could perform 18 different commands, see, hear, and interact with amazed exhibition audiences. The VDNKH robot represented the Soviet Union's early venture into humanoid robotics and technological showmanship. Developed by young technicians under Boris Vasilenko's guidance, these robots were designed to demonstrate Soviet technological capabilities at the famous VDNKH exhibition center in Moscow. The most advanced model stood 1.8 meters tall and could execute 18 different commands via radio control, including movement, gesture recognition, and basic interaction. These robots featured primitive vision and hearing capabilities using sensors to detect light and sound for responsive behavior. The VDNKH robots performed every two hours on a special stage built in front of the electrification pavilion, drawing crowds of amazed visitors. Beyond their mechanical functions, these robots symbolized Soviet optimism about the future, representing a vision where automation would support human progress. The project combined engineering innovation with theatrical presentation, capturing public imagination about human-machine collaboration. Soviet robotics development extended beyond exhibitions. By 1980, the USSR operated over 6,000 industrial robots, representing more than 20% of the world's total. The country pioneered planetary rovers, developing the first lunar rovers and Mars exploration vehicles. While primitive by modern standards, the VDNKH robots played a significant role in robotics history, demonstrating early concepts of autonomous behavior and human-robot interaction that would influence future development.

answer: Seeing a red light on your AirPods Pro 3 charging case, it's a signal from the case's LED indicator about the charging or battery status. A solid red light usually means the case battery is critically low, below 10%, and needs charging. If you see a flashing red light, this often indicates a charging error, potentially due to a faulty lightning port, incompatible charger, or an internal issue. While charging, the light should turn amber/orange, indicating normal charging, and then green when fully charged. Basically, the red light is a diagnostic indicator to alert you of a problem with power or charging. If you encounter a red light, first try resetting your AirPods via the Bluetooth settings on your paired device. Next, clean the charging port with a soft dry brush to remove any debris that might be interfering with the connection. Then, use a different charging cable and adapter. Ideally, use Apple's USB-C to lightning adapter as the Pro 3 supports both lightning and USB-C magsafe. Also, ensure your AirPods Pro 3 firmware is up to date via your paired iOS device. If the red light persists, it might indicate a hardware fault. In that case, contact Apple support or an authorized service provider, especially if the device is still under warranty, which has been extended to two years in some cases due to reported manufacturing defects.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: In April 1976, six years after the Beatles' official breakup, an unusual moment in television history nearly triggered a legendary reunion. Lorne Michaels, the newly appointed producer of Saturday Night Live, made a bold and humorous pitch during a live broadcast. Looking straight into the camera, he offered the Beatles $3,000 to reunite on the SNL stage and perform three of their classic songs. Holding up a check, Michaels jokingly added that the money could be split however they wished, even suggesting that if they felt Ringo Starr didn't deserve an equal share, they were free to divide the funds accordingly. The proposal was clearly meant as satire, but fatefully, two of the Beatles, John Lennon and Paul McCartney, were watching the show that very night. McCartney happened to be visiting Lennon at his Dakota apartment in New York City, only a short cab ride away from the NBC studio. According to various sources, including Tom Doyle's Man on the Run, the two icons laughed heartily at Michael's stunt. Lennon, amused, turned to McCartney and suggested, half-jokingly, "Should we go down there and just do it?" They were reportedly close to calling a cab, but ultimately decided against it, citing the late hour and their desire to relax. It was a near miss that fans have since romanticized as the Beatles reunion that almost happened. Although Lennon and McCartney didn't follow through, the moment lived on as a curious what if in pop culture. Later that year, George Harrison appeared on SNL's cold open. In a scripted bit, he confronted Lorne Michaels to claim the $3,000. Michaels explained deadpan that the offer was intended for all four members and that Harrison alone was only entitled to $750. Harrison, staying in character, haggled for an extra $250 if he agreed to say the famous line, "Live from New York, it's Saturday night." This whimsical series of events has become a cherished anecdote among Beatles fans, capturing a moment when a spontaneous, lighthearted invitation nearly brought together two of the world's most influential musicians. It stands as a testament to the Beatles' enduring presence in the public imagination and how even the most casual of gestures can ripple through music history.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Your AI agents are burning tokens like crazy and it's not your prompt's fault. It's the architecture. Anthropic just dropped the biggest update yet, MCP code execution, and it changes everything about how agents work and can save up to 98% tokens. I'll explain what's new, why MCP needed this upgrade, and I'll show you a real demo that anyone can run locally. Typically, every MCP server exposes 10 to 20 tools. Every tool comes with function description, parameters, types, examples that translates into tens of thousands of tokens. All irrelevant for 90% of tasks. And this is where accuracy drops because the model is drowning in noise. It keeps confusing tools, mixing parameters, hallucinating schema fields, and failing mid-workflow. This is the new mental model behind MCP. Instead of dumping every tool definition into the model's context window, tools appears as a file system. To get the exact estimates, I generated a synthetic cloud watch style data set that looks exactly like what real DevOps engineers deal with. So, it has data for 150 EC2 instances. Each instance has 50 to 150 CPU data points. What the script does is loads the entire data set as raw text. This means all 18,000 data points become part of the prompt. The LLM has to read the entire JSON block. This turns into 355,000 tokens, which is almost double of what the token limit of the LLM is, and ultimately the LLM is choked. It throws a quota exceeded error where the limit is just 125,000 tokens. Now, let's take a look at the MCP style flow, where the model doesn't touch the data set. We filter the data set locally. The local Python finds the high CPU instances. Only the tiny summary is passed into the model. Gemini responds instantly. Token usage drops from 355,000 to 2096. That's more than 98% token savings. And this is the magic. The LLM sees only the result, not the 18,000 data points. This is why MCP code execution is such a big deal. Instead of forcing LLMs to parse huge tool definitions and giant JSON blobs, we let the model write code on which it is exclusively trained on, and we only give it the tiny slice of data it actually needs. Let me know in the comments what you think about MCP code execution. See you in the next video.
